title: Authentication Login UI Journey
description: Draft UI semantic model instance for the login journey, separate from visual styling, component composition, source JSX structure, screenshots, and generated reports. The first UI assurance slice governs login journey states, validation, explicit error handling, permission-gated surfaces, accessibility requirements, user actions, and semantic interface invocation before implementation extraction. This record is a semantic input for future UI generation only; it does not claim product UI readiness, browser E2E readiness, staging readiness, production readiness, or live-provider readiness.
aiGuidance: Regenerate UI from semantics; do not invent validation, permission, accessibility, composition, layout hierarchy, or journey behaviour from visual design, JSX layout, component names, screenshots, or generated reports. Preserve the non-claim boundary: this semantic model is not a product UI readiness, browser E2E readiness, staging readiness, production readiness, or live-provider readiness claim.

journeys.name: Login attempt
steps: receive authenticated, denied, provider-failure, no-session, or auth-error retry state

journeys.name: Authentication error retry
steps: invoke governed login interface handoff on retry

journeys.name: Permission gated surface
steps: evaluate required permission from semantic permission context
render forbidden state when permission is absent
avoid exposing gated control as enabled when permission is absent

validations: required login input is represented before submission
provider selection or login handoff is represented before redirect or callback handling
retry action preserves generic error semantics and does not expose raw provider error details
custom-domain callback origin is represented as source-backed lineage, not live-provider proof
deferred real-IdP claim mapping is visible as a readiness limitation
session query result is represented before permission-gated controls are shown as available
permission checks are semantic permission checks and not visual hiding alone
errors: generic auth-error state is explicit and retryable
no-session state redirects or blocks authenticated surfaces
forbidden state is explicit for missing permissions
stale proof or readiness failure cannot be shown as ready
accessibility: error state is announced without relying on visual styling only
auth-error retry control has an accessible name
forbidden state communicates denied access without relying on colour or layout only
keyboard interaction reaches login and retry actions
